transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-10
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: 48 mins
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Ivy Chen (Redwood CSM), Jordan Li (Corelytics Legal), Maya Thompson (Corelytics FinOps), Rafael Gomez (Corelytics Platform), Priya Nair (Corelytics Security)
---
Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be rough): Corelytics wants to understand what concessions, if any, Redwood can make on the MSA/DPA for a pilot, how SLA credits would be applied, and how pricing for committed vs burst capacity would look. They also need KMS integration details and a short performance run before procurement signs off.
---
00:00 Lena Park: hi everyone, thanks for joining, i'm lena from redwood, we have samir and ivy on the line, and you all, thanks for making time. quick run of agenda, legal redlines, sla/pricing, k m s questions, and pilot timeline.
00:22 Jordan Li: thanks lena, yep, we'll be tight on time today so i'll jump in on the legal points quickly. our procurement team flagged two main asks — limited retention for certain logs in the d p a, and a tighter SLA credit for p99 outages during pilot.
00:40 Maya Thompson: and on the finops side we need committed volume pricing vs burst, and clarity on egress mapping to get budget approval.
00:50 Samir Patel: understood — from an eng perspective we also need to confirm whether dedicated is required for their use-case or if vpc-hosted can meet the residency and isolation asks. i can run a quick benchmark with sample traffic.
01:10 Rafael Gomez: just to clarify, our data classification says some inference logs are regulated, not full PII but metadata that must be retained in-region. so residency matters.
01:30 Priya Nair: security here — we need customer-managed keys for the privileged paths and controls on key rotation, plus an audit log for key usage. is that supported in private deployment?
01:45 Samir Patel: yes we support customer-managed KMS in Private deployments today, and in Dedicated we can integrate with a customer KMS via our key plugin. for hosted, there are limited options — we normally provide envelope encryption but we can discuss an HSM-backed flow as an exception.
02:10 Jordan Li: okay, that's helpful. legally, the DPA redline we've proposed removes certain broad retention windows and instead gates retention on purpose and scope. we're also asking for a more favorable SLA credit-tier for the pilot period. is that something you can accept?
02:30 Lena Park: we treat pilots differently — we can be flexible on retention windows for pilot data, but we need to balance that with our operational traceability. proposal: 90 day reduced retention for pilot diagnostic logs with an explicit deletion process. for SLA credits, we can offer an escalated point-of-contact and a 10% credit cap during pilot instead of normal 20% if the pilot shows low incident frequency.
03:02 Jordan Li: 90 days is reasonable, but legal will want that in writing as a DPA addendum. and 10% cap — we need to confirm that final figure with procurement leadership.
03:20 Maya Thompson: on pricing — can you show committed monthly tokens versus on-demand? we have a seasonal burst in Q3 so we need a model that doesn't blow the budget.
03:40 Samir Patel: sure — high level, three tiers: on-demand per-token; committed with a flat discount for baseline and burst pricing for overage; and dedicated reserved pool where you prepay for capacity. i'll prepare three scenarios with numbers, but we should align on expected baseline tokens for the pilot.
04:05 Rafael Gomez: for pilot, we expect about 50M tokens / month to start, rising to 150M in a month if the beta goes well.
04:20 Samir Patel: perfect — i'll run bench sims at those loadpoints. for p99 latency we need the target — what do you expect?
04:35 Rafael Gomez: sub-250ms on average, 95% under 400ms. we understand some tail will be higher.
04:50 Samir Patel: that's achievable with dedicated pools and our batching config; for hosted we'd need to tune caching aggressively and might see higher variance.
05:10 Jordan Li: i have a specific ask — could we get a provision that logs with regulated flags are never exported for analytics outside EEA? basically a data residency safeguard.
05:30 Priya Nair: yes and also proof of audit logs (who accessed keys, when) — we need those shipping for the security review.
05:45 Samir Patel: we can map logs by tag and enforce egress region rules in Dedicated and Private. Hosted can be region-restricted but we'd need the DPA addendum to state that. for audit logs, we can provide syslog/S3 delivery or SFTP pull with retention policy.
06:10 Lena Park: legal's point on SLA credits — we can do a pilot-specific SLA schedule in the SOW, that gets appended to the MSA. it's not unusual. the concession on credit cap is something we can tentatively accept pending exec signoff.
06:35 Jordan Li: exec signoff is the rub — if procurement wants a lower cap they'll need a commercial exception. can you outline how often exceptions like that are granted?
06:50 Lena Park: exceptions happen for strategic customers and pilots; we surface them to our sales finance and legal team. i'll put together the business case and run it up for you.
07:05 Maya Thompson: timeline wise — we'd like to have pilot running in 3 weeks, legal sign-off in 2, and procurement after bench results. is that realistic?
07:20 Samir Patel: technically, a 1-week bench + 1-week integration and 1-week stabilization is doable. if legal can sign DPA addendum in 2 weeks then yes.
07:35 Jordan Li: we need the redlines diff to iterate quickly. can you send a tracked changes doc?
07:45 Lena Park: yes, i'll send the redlines diff, and i'll highlight the pilot concessions.
07:55 Rafael Gomez: one more technical — how do rollbacks work if we see model regressions? we need automatic fallback to a previous model variant.
08:12 Samir Patel: automatic fallback is supported; we can stage a canary for each rollout and define rollback policies. we'll include rollback SLOs in the SOW.
08:30 Priya Nair: about key rotation — we rotate every 90 days internally, customer needs to state rotation policy. is live rotation supported?
08:45 Samir Patel: yes, live rekey is supported with minimal interruption using double-wrap approach; we'll document the expected window.
09:00 Jordan Li: ok, to summarize legal asks: a DPA addendum limiting retention for pilot logs to 90 days, explicit data residency clause for regulated logs, and pilot-specific SLA schedule with credit cap.
09:18 Lena Park: correct. next steps: i'll send the MSA/DPA redline diff; samir will schedule bench run; customer will send any procurement templates.
09:35 Maya Thompson: and financials — please include committed vs burst scenarios and example invoice math so we can run the models.
09:45 Samir Patel: noted, i'll include 3 scenarios and break down expected unit costs with caching and quantization options.
09:58 Jordan Li: any blockers on our side — we need to check whether the keying model requires additional procurement approval if an HSM vendor is involved.
10:10 Priya Nair: we'll confirm.
10:20 Ivy Chen: i'll follow up on onboarding checklist and schedule weekly syncs during pilot.
10:30 Lena Park: great — thanks everyone. shall we capture final recap and agree on dates?
10:40 Jordan Li: yep.
